posts.title: Arrests rise to 1,800 in France
posts.text: More than 1,800 people have been arrested in France over protests on Saturday, the country’s interior minister Laurent Nunez has said. Nunez, in a post on X, said “the Republic will not yield” as more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters have been injured in the demonstrations. “The material damage is…

It’s important to note that protests have also been taking place across Europe. In Italy rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property on fire in central Milan on Saturday. The demonstration escalated after a march against wars and rising living costs began peacefully. However masked protesters threw…

Here’s a selection of photographs from the protests on Saturday and their aftermath, including the City Hall in Limoges. The prefect on Sunday said the blaze in the 143-year-old building had been contained.

In case you are still catching up with the news from yesterday, my colleagues Kim Willsher and William Christou have this report. More than 1,200 people were arrested in France on Saturday after protesters supporting high school students clashed with police, with some demonstrations later spiralling out of control as…

posts.title: Record numbers arrested in Paris
posts.text: Police in Paris arrested a “record figure” of 855 people during the protests on Saturday. Agence France-Presse reported the number detained was the highest ever for a single event. The figure forms part of the 1,200 arrested across France, as prime minister Sébastien Lecornu said 150 police had been hurt in clashes.…

posts.text: France is recovering after its worst protests in years saw buildings attacked and set ablaze across the country.
